roleContext.roleTitle: Credit Risk Data Scientist, Consumer Lending
roleContext.jobDescription: A consumer lender offering personal loans and credit cards builds its own application and behavioural scorecards. The Credit Risk Data Scientist develops and monitors scorecards, prepares model documentation for independent validation, produces the quarterly IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss inputs and works with the credit policy team on cut-off changes. The quarter-end close week often involves extended hours. The credit risk analytics team has seven people and reports to the chief risk officer through the head of credit risk analytics. Scorecards are built in Python and SAS, documented to the lender's model risk standard and reviewed by an independent validation team before use. The IFRS 9 inputs go to the finance team by the fourth working day after quarter-end.

requirements.text: Produces the quarterly IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss inputs to the finance deadline in the close week.
Develops application or behavioural scorecards using logistic regression or gradient boosting.
Monitors scorecard performance with stability and discrimination metrics each month.
Prepares model documentation that passes independent model validation.
Analyses the effect of proposed cut-off changes with the credit policy team.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Credit Risk Data Scientist, Consumer Lending

## Experience

- Developed a behavioural scorecard for the credit-card book at Redbrook Finance with logistic regression on 30 months of performance data, replacing a vendor score.
- Produced the monthly monitoring pack for five scorecards: Gini, population stability index and characteristic analysis, with an amber or red flag for each breach of the agreed thresholds.
- Leave of absence, April to November 2023: cancer treatment, followed by a phased return to full-time hours.
- Wrote the development documentation for the behavioural scorecard, which the independent model validation team approved with two minor findings.
- Ran swap-set analyses for three proposed cut-off changes, showing the credit policy team the expected approvals and bad rates under each option.

## Work samples

- Work sample: an anonymised monthly monitoring pack for one scorecard, with the Gini trend, the population stability index by month and a characteristic analysis for the two drifting variables.
